title: Canonical module localization and exact stalk presentations of affine cohomology
statement: For a commutative ring A, an integer i and a derived object L with quasi-coherent cohomology on Spec A [def-pc-derived-category], define T_i(L) as the actual global sections of H^i(L) [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. At every prime p, the canonical global-section germ map and the tilde/Gamma counit identify T_i(L)_p with the stalk H^i(L)_p [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization]. This additive equivalence is natural for every derived morphism between quasi-coherent objects. For any complex P of module sheaves on any scheme Y, exact stalks identify the stalk of H^i(QP) with H^i(P_p), naturally for chain maps [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact].

proof.text: Take global sections of the actual cohomology sheaf. Its quasi-coherence makes fromTildeΓ invertible. Compose IsLocalizedModule.iso for the germ map with the stalk of this counit; forget scalars to obtain affineDerivedCohomologyStalkIso.

Prove naturality of tilde stalk maps on germs using tilde.toOpen_map_app. The universal localization property gives equality with IsLocalizedModule.map; map_iso_commute transports this across the localization equivalences. Apply naturality of fromTildeΓNatTrans to finish the square. This is all proved in Lean.

Use module_stalk_exact to establish PreservesHomology. Compose the stalk of homologyFunctorFactors with the inverse short-complex mapHomologyIso. Naturality of both factors proves affineRepresentativeStalkIso_naturality.
